content: For the treatment of brain abscesses in otherwise healthy patients, the preferred regimen includes either cefotaxime at a dosage of 8–12 g per day administered intravenously every 4–6 hours or ceftriaxone at a dosage of 4 g per day administered intravenously every 12 hours, combined with metronidazole at 30 mg/kg/day administered intravenously every 6 hours. An alternative regimen involves meropenem at 6 g per day administered intravenously every 8 hours. For brain abscesses associated with otitis media, mastoiditis, or sinusitis, the preferred treatment is the same as for otherwise healthy patients: cefotaxime or ceftriaxone combined with metronidazole. For brain abscesses resulting from dental infections, the preferred regimen is penicillin G at 4 million units administered intravenously every 4 hours, combined with metronidazole at 30 mg/kg/day administered intravenously every 6 hours. In cases of brain abscesses caused by penetrating trauma or post-neurosurgical procedures, the preferred regimen includes either cefotaxime (8–12 g/day IV q4–6h), ceftriaxone (4 g/day IV q12h), or cefepime (2 g IV q12h), combined with vancomycin at 30–45 mg/kg/day administered intravenously every 8–12 hours. For brain abscesses associated with lung abscess, empyema, or bronchiectasis, the preferred regimen includes penicillin G (4 million units IV q4h), metronidazole (30 mg/kg/day IV q6h), and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMZ) at 10–20 mg/kg/day administered intravenously every 6–12 hours. For brain abscesses related to bacterial endocarditis, the preferred treatment is vancomycin at 30–45 mg/kg/day administered intravenously every 8–12 hours, combined with gentamicin at 5 mg/kg/day administered intravenously every 8 hours. In patients with congenital heart disease, the preferred regimen is either cefotaxime (8–12 g/day IV q4–6h) or ceftriaxone (4 g/day IV q12h). For transplant recipients with brain abscesses, the preferred regimen includes cefotaxime (8–12 g/day IV q4–6h) or ceftriaxone (4 g/day IV q12h), combined with metronidazole (30 mg/kg/day IV q6h), voriconazole (8 mg/kg/day IV q12h), and either TMP-SMZ (10–20 mg/kg/day IV q6–12h) or sulfadiazine (4–6 g/day IV q6h). For patients with HIV/AIDS, the preferred regimen includes cefotaxime (8–12 g/day IV q4–6h) or ceftriaxone (4 g/day IV q12h), combined with sulfadiazine (4–6 g/day IV q6h) and pyrimethamine (25–100 mg/day orally once daily). For coverage of Staphylococcus aureus, the preferred regimen is vancomycin at 30–45 mg/kg/day administered intravenously every 8–12 hours. For coverage of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the preferred regimen includes isoniazid (300 mg orally once daily), rifampin (600 mg orally once daily), pyrazinamide (15–30 mg/kg orally once daily), and ethambutol (15 mg/kg/day orally once daily). For pathogen-directed therapy: For Actinomyces, the preferred regimen is penicillin G (4 million units IV q4h), with clindamycin (2400–4800 mg/day IV q6h) as an alternative. For Bacteroides fragilis, the preferred regimen is metronidazole (30 mg/kg/day IV q6h), with clindamycin (2400–4800 mg/day IV q6h) as an alternative. For Enterobacteriaceae, the preferred regimen includes cefotaxime (2 g IV q4–6h), ceftriaxone (2 g IV q12h), or cefepime (2 g IV q12h). Alternatives include aztreonam (6–8 g/day IV q6–8h), TMP-SMZ (10–20 mg/kg/day IV q6–12h), ciprofloxacin (800–1200 mg/day IV q8–12h), or meropenem (2 g IV q8h). For Fusobacterium, the preferred regimen is metronidazole (30 mg/kg/day IV q6h), with clindamycin (2400–4800 mg/day IV q6h) or meropenem (2 g IV q8h) as alternatives. For Haemophilus, the preferred regimen includes cefotaxime (2 g IV q4–6h), ceftriaxone (2 g IV q12h), or cefepime (2 g IV q12h). Alternatives include aztreonam (6–8 g/day IV q6–8h) or TMP-SMZ (10–20 mg/kg/day IV q6–12h). For Listeria monocytogenes, the preferred regimen is ampicillin (12 g/day IV q4h) or penicillin G (4 million units IV q4h), with TMP-SMZ (10–20 mg/kg/day IV q6–12h) as an alternative. For Nocardia, the preferred regimen includes TMP-SMZ (10–20 mg/kg/day IV q6–12h) or sulfadiazine (4–6 g/day IV q6h). Alternatives include meropenem (2 g IV q8h), cefotaxime (2 g IV q4–6h), ceftriaxone (2 g IV q12h), or amikacin (15 mg/kg/day IV q8h). For Prevotella melaninogenica, the preferred regimen is metronidazole (30 mg/kg/day IV q6h), with clindamycin (2400–4800 mg/day IV q6h) or meropenem (2 g IV q8h) as alternatives. For Pseudomonas aeruginosa, the preferred regimen includes ceftazidime (6 g/day IV q8h) or cefepime (6 g/day IV q8h). Alternatives include aztreonam (6–8 g/day IV q6–8h), ciprofloxacin (800–1200 mg/day IV q8–12h), or meropenem (2 g IV q8h). For methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus, the preferred regimen is nafcillin (2 g IV q4h) or oxacillin (2 g IV q4h), with vancomycin (30–45 mg/kg/day IV q8–12h) as an alternative. For methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, the preferred regimen is vancomycin (30–45 mg/kg/day IV q8–12h), with TMP-SMZ (10–20 mg/kg/day IV q6–12h) as an alternative. For Streptococcus, the preferred regimen is penicillin G (4 million units IV q4h) or ampicillin (2 g IV q4h), with cefotaxime (2 g IV q4–6h), ceftriaxone (2 g IV q12h), or vancomycin (30–45 mg/kg/day IV q8–12h) as alternatives. For fungal infections: For Aspergillus, the preferred regimen is voriconazole (8 mg/kg/day IV q12h). Alternatives include amphotericin B deoxycholate (0.6–1.0 mg/kg/day IV q24h), amphotericin B lipid complex (5 mg/kg/day IV q24h), itraconazole (400–600 mg/day IV q12h), or posaconazole (800 mg/day IV q6–12h). For Candida, the preferred regimen includes amphotericin B lipid complex (5 mg/kg/day IV q24h) or amphotericin B deoxycholate (15 mg/kg/day IV q8h). Fluconazole (400–800 mg/day IV q24h) is an alternative. For Cryptococcus neoformans, the preferred regimen includes amphotericin B lipid complex (5 mg/kg/day IV q24h) or amphotericin B deoxycholate (15 mg/kg/day IV q8h). Fluconazole (400–800 mg/day IV q24h) is an alternative. For Mucorales, the preferred regimen includes amphotericin B lipid complex (5 mg/kg/day IV q24h) or amphotericin B deoxycholate (15 mg/kg/day IV q8h). Posaconazole (800 mg/day IV q6–12h) is an alternative. For Pseudallescheria boydii (Scedosporium apiospermum), the preferred regimen is voriconazole (8 mg/kg/day IV q12h). Alternatives include itraconazole (400–600 mg/day IV q12h) or posaconazole (800 mg/day IV q6–12h). For protozoal infections: For Toxoplasma gondii, the preferred regimen includes sulfadiazine (4–6 g/day IV q6h) and pyrimethamine (25–100 mg/day orally once daily). Alternative regimens include pyrimethamine combined with clindamycin (2400–4800 mg/day IV q6h), azithromycin (1200–1500 mg/day IV q24h), atovaquone (750 mg IV q6h), or dapsone (100 mg orally q24h). TMP-SMZ (10–20 mg/kg/day IV q6–12h) is another alternative.
